summary: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
detail: Irrational and transcendental: it never ends and never repeats. Archimedes bounded it by 223/71 < π < 22/7; it is now known to over 100 trillion digits.
source: Mathematical constant (used by the engine as pi or π)

summary: Base of the natural logarithm, about 2.71828.
detail: Defined as the limit of (1 + 1/n)^n as n grows, or as the value where the curve y = e^x has slope 1. It appears wherever growth or decay is proportional to size.

summary: The circle constant equal to 2π, about 6.28319.
detail: One full turn in radians. Some authors prefer τ because formulas like C = τr and ω = τf have no stray factor of two.

summary: The number (1 + √5)/2 ≈ 1.618, the ratio at which a line divided into two parts satisfies the whole:long = long:short.
The set of points at a fixed distance (the radius) from a centre.
detail: Area = πr², circumference = 2πr. A circle is not a polygon, so its perimeter has no straight-sided approximation.

summary: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides: a² + b² = c².
detail: The basis of Euclidean distance, and the reason the diagonal of a unit square is √2 — a length no fraction can measure exactly.

summary: The solutions of ax² + bx + c = 0 are x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a.
detail: The part under the root, b² − 4ac, is the discriminant: positive gives two real roots, zero one repeated root, negative a complex conjugate pair.

summary: For ax² + bx + c, the quantity b² − 4ac that decides how many real roots the equation has.
The instantaneous rate at which a function changes — the slope of its graph at a point.
detail: Written f'(x) or dy/dx, defined as the limit of (f(x+h) − f(x))/h as h → 0. Differentiating x² gives 2x, sin x gives cos x, and eˣ is its own derivative.

summary: The accumulated total of a function — the area under its graph between two limits.
detail: The fundamental theorem of calculus links it to the derivative: differentiating an integral returns the original function. The engine evaluates definite integrals numerically (adaptive Simpson).

summary: The value a function approaches as its input approaches a point, whether or not the function is defined there.
detail: lim(x→0) sin x / x = 1 even though the expression is 0/0 at x = 0. Limits define both the derivative and the integral.

summary: The product of all whole numbers from 1 to n; 0! is defined as 1.
detail: Grows fast: 20! is about 2.43 × 10^18. The engine is exact up to 170!; beyond that the float result overflows.

summary: The sequence 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, … where each term is the sum of the two before it.
detail: The ratio of consecutive terms approaches the golden ratio φ ≈ 1.618, and the sequence counts many natural patterns such as spirals in shells.

summary: A whole number greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself.
detail: There are infinitely many primes (Euclid). Every whole number above 1 factors into primes in exactly one way — the fundamental theorem of arithmetic.

summary: A comparison of two quantities by division, written a : b or a/b.
detail: Ratios scale: 2 : 3 is the same as 20 : 30. A proportion is a statement that two ratios are equal.

summary: A fraction expressed out of 100: 25% means 25/100 = 0.25.
detail: In the engine the postfix operator % divides by 100, so 50% is 0.5 and 200 * 10% is 20.

summary: The sum of a set of values divided by how many there are.
detail: Sensitive to outliers: one very large value pulls the mean far above the median.

summary: The middle value once the data are ordered; with an even count, the mean of the two middle values.
detail: Unlike the mean, the median is barely affected by extreme values, which is why house prices and incomes are usually reported as medians.

summary: A measure of how spread out values are around the mean, in the same units as the data.
detail: The square root of the variance. For a normal distribution about 68% of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean and 95% within two.

summary: The average squared distance of values from their mean.
detail: Squared units make it hard to read directly, which is why its square root — the standard deviation — is usually quoted. The sample version divides by n − 1.

summary: The symmetric bell-shaped distribution described by its mean μ and standard deviation σ.
detail: The total probability inside ±1σ is about 0.6827, inside ±2σ about 0.9545, and inside ±3σ about 0.9973.

summary: The angle subtended at a circle's centre by an arc equal in length to the radius; a full turn is 2π radians.
detail: 1 radian = 180/π ≈ 57.2958°. Radians make derivative formulas clean (d/dx sin x = cos x), which is why science works in them.
source: SI derived unit for plane angle

summary: An angle unit equal to 1/360 of a full turn.
detail: 360 was chosen by Babylonian astronomers because it divides evenly by many numbers. One degree = π/180 radians ≈ 0.0174533 rad.

summary: A rectangular array of numbers, used to represent linear transformations, systems of equations and data.
detail: An m × n matrix has m rows and n columns. Multiplication is only defined when the inner dimensions match, and it is not commutative: AB ≠ BA in general.

summary: A single number computed from a square matrix that tells you whether it scales volumes and whether it can be inverted.
detail: Zero determinant means the matrix is singular — it collapses space onto a smaller dimension and has no inverse. For a 2×2 matrix, det = ad − bc.

summary: A scalar λ such that a matrix only stretches, never rotates, the eigenvector it acts on: Av = λv.
detail: Eigenvalues drive vibration modes, principal-component analysis, Markov chain behaviour and stability analysis of dynamic systems.

summary: The power you must raise a base to in order to get a number: log₁₀(1000) = 3.
detail: ln is the logarithm base e. In the engine log(x) is base 10 and log(x, b) is base b; ln(x) is base e.

summary: The function eˣ, which grows at a rate proportional to its own value.
detail: Its derivative equals itself, so it describes unchecked growth (populations early on, compound interest) and radioactive decay when the exponent is negative.

summary: Interest calculated on the initial amount plus all previously earned interest, so growth accelerates.
detail: A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) for n compounds per year, or Pe^(rt) for continuous compounding.

summary: Interest calculated only on the original principal: I = Prt.
The steepness of a line: the vertical change divided by the horizontal change.
detail: For a curve the gradient at a point is the derivative there. A line with gradient 2 rises two units for every one across.

summary: The value that appears most often in a data set.
detail: A data set can have several modes or none. It is the only average that also works for categories such as favourite colours.

summary: A quantity with both size and direction, written as an ordered list of components.
detail: The magnitude of (x, y, z) is √(x² + y² + z²). The dot product measures alignment and the cross product gives a perpendicular vector.

summary: The sum of the products of matching components: (1,2,3)·(4,5,6) = 32. It equals |a||b|cos θ.
detail: Zero dot product means the vectors are perpendicular; the dot product with a unit vector gives a projected length.

summary: A vector perpendicular to both inputs, with magnitude equal to the area of the parallelogram they span.
As x approaches 0, sin x / x approaches 1 — the foundation of small-angle approximations.
detail: Used throughout physics: for small angles sin θ ≈ θ (in radians), which makes pendulums and lenses tractable.

summary: The agreed order for evaluating an expression: brackets, indices (powers and roots), then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction.
detail: OmniCalc follows this order, and applies implicit multiplication at the same level as division, so 1/2x is (1/2)·x.

summary: The digits in a number that carry meaning about its precision.
detail: Leading zeros never count; trailing zeros after a decimal point do. A result should not be quoted to more significant figures than its least precise input.

summary: Replacing a number with a nearby simpler one, usually to a given number of decimal places or significant figures.
detail: Standard rounding looks at the next digit: 5 or more rounds up. 'Round half to even' (banker's rounding) avoids a systematic upward bias in large sums.

summary: A number of the form a + bi, where i is the square root of −1.
detail: Complex numbers make every polynomial solvable and describe oscillations, AC circuits, signal processing and quantum states.

summary: The number i with i² = −1, which makes the square root of any negative number definable.
detail: Powers of i cycle every four: i, −1, −i, 1.

summary: e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ, linking exponentials to trigonometry.
detail: Setting θ = π gives Euler's identity e^(iπ) + 1 = 0, which ties together five fundamental constants.

summary: An arrangement where order matters: the number of ways to choose and order r items from n is n!/(n−r)!.
A selection where order does not matter: nCr = n!/(r!(n−r)!).
detail: There are 13 983 816 ways to choose 6 numbers from 49 — which is why lottery odds are so long.

summary: A number between 0 and 1 saying how likely an event is; P = favourable outcomes / total outcomes for equally likely cases.
detail: Probabilities of independent events multiply; of mutually exclusive events add. Zero means impossible, one means certain.

summary: The ratio of the probability of an event to the probability of it not happening: p : (1 − p).
detail: Odds of 3:1 mean p = 0.75. Bookmakers quote odds that include their margin, so they are not the true probabilities.

summary: The value below which a given percentage of the data falls; the 90th percentile is above 90% of values.
detail: The median is the 50th percentile and Q1/Q3 are the 25th and 75th.

summary: The three values that split ordered data into four equal parts: Q1 (25%), Q2/median (50%), Q3 (75%).
Q3 − Q1: the spread of the middle half of the data, unaffected by outliers.
How many standard deviations a value lies from the mean: z = (x − μ)/σ.
detail: z = 1.96 marks the central 95% of a normal distribution, which is why 1.96 appears in confidence intervals.

summary: The probability of seeing data at least as extreme as observed, if the null hypothesis were true.
detail: A small p value is evidence against the null hypothesis — not proof of the alternative, and not the probability that the null is true.

summary: A number from −1 to 1 describing how closely two variables move together on a straight line.
detail: Correlation is not causation: ice-cream sales correlate with drowning deaths because both rise in hot weather.

summary: The fraction of the variation in the outcome explained by a fitted model, from 0 to 1.
detail: R² = 0.9 means 90% of the variation is explained. Adding more predictors always raises it, so adjusted R² is used for comparison.

summary: Fitting a line (or curve) that best explains how one variable changes with another, usually by least squares.
detail: Least squares minimises the sum of squared vertical distances from the points. The slope is the change in y per unit change in x.

summary: A line that a curve approaches ever more closely without reaching.
detail: y = 1/x has asymptotes at x = 0 and y = 0. In the app, evaluating exactly on a vertical asymptote is reported as a domain error rather than a huge number.

summary: A rule that assigns exactly one output to each input.
detail: Written f(x). Plotting a function shows every input–output pair; a vertical line must never cut the graph twice.

summary: The domain is the set of allowed inputs; the range is the set of outputs actually produced.
detail: √x has domain x ≥ 0 and range y ≥ 0. OmniCalc reports values outside the domain as errors instead of returning a complex approximation.

summary: A symbol standing for a value that can change, such as x in a formula.
detail: An unknown is a variable whose value is to be found by solving; a parameter is fixed for the problem but can vary between problems.

summary: A statement that one quantity is larger or smaller than another, using <, ≤, > or ≥.
detail: Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number flips the direction of the sign.

summary: An equation whose graph is a straight line, such as y = mx + c.
detail: m is the gradient (steepness) and c the y-intercept where it crosses the y-axis.

summary: Two or more equations that must all hold at once, solved for the shared unknowns.
detail: If there are as many independent equations as unknowns there is usually one solution; parallel lines give none, and the same line twice gives infinitely many.

summary: The U-shaped curve of a quadratic function y = ax² + bx + c.
detail: It opens upwards when a > 0 and downwards when a < 0. Its vertex is the minimum (or maximum), found at x = −b/2a.

summary: The point where a graph crosses the y-axis — the value of y when x is 0.
